A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 36-page study, including Appendices A–C. Pages 2–36 match exactly in extracted text and rendered appearance; the first-page research content also matches.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual mathematical-reasoning experiments, including scaling comparisons, trained-model evaluations in Table 4, and training ablations in Appendix B.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Table 4, Appendix B.2's ablations, and Appendix C's detailed per-language evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 5 retain identical ORM, PRM and budget-forcing procedures, along with the same multilingual fine-tuning and MR1-1.5B training approach.

E1.justification: The four MCLM subsets and their language coverage are unchanged (Table 2; Appendix A.1). Training datasets and additional appendix evaluation scenarios also match.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. For example, Table 4 retains the same Qwen2.5-Math, Deepseek-R1, GPT-4o-Mini, o3-Mini and fine-tuned model entries.

E3.justification: The compute-matching configurations, token budgets and evaluation metrics in Section 3 and Table 3 are identical. Sampling and training settings in Appendices A–B also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The PRM step, candidate-count and verifier-size analyses, MATH100 sampling validation in Appendix A.2, and multilingual training ablations in Appendix B.2 are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Cross-language standard deviations and error-bar reporting are identical in Table 4, Figure 8 and Appendix C. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All main-text and appendix result entries match. Figure 1 retains average scores of 35.84 for ORM, 29.35 for PRM and 35.23 for MT-SFT + BF.

T1.justification: The inference-FLOPs equations in Section 3.2 and cross-lingual consistency formulation in Section 3.3 are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations or other theoretical material change.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same contributions and headline claims concerning MCLM, MR1-1.5B, comparable budget-matched scaling performance, and limited cross-lingual generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of multilingual scaling and qualifications about mathematical tasks, small models, limited compute and possible benchmark contamination remain unchanged, including the Limitations section and Appendix A.5.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, training time, hyperparameters, data preparation, prompt templates, licenses and code/data links are unchanged. Appendix B.3 and Table 10 contain identical training disclosures.

R1.justification: Section 6, the bibliography and research-positioning statements are identical. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv label changes from v1 dated 24 Feb 2025 to v2 dated 1 Aug 2025 and gains a self-link. PDF title/author metadata is populated, while the visible title, authors, prose and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Only the first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned. Figures 1–15, Tables 1–26, captions and the layout of all research content remain identical.

improvement.justification: The research narrative, experimental evidence, technical disclosures, limitations and appendices are unchanged. Updating the arXiv stamp, metadata and self-link produces no meaningful overall improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
